title: colombia 12 month inflation edges up more than expected august 2026 09 07
text:
BOGOTA, Sept 7 (Reuters) - Colombia's consumer prices rose 0.39% in August, the country's DANE statistics ​agency said on Monday, taking annual price ‌growth to 6.24%.
The August figure was above the 0.26% median forecast of analysts polled by Reuters, ​and higher than the 0.17% recorded in ​July.
Annual inflation edged up from 6.03% in ⁠July and came in just above the ​6.10% forcast by analysts.
Inflation remains well above ​the central bank's target of 3% plus or minus one percentage point.
The monthly increases were led by recreation ​and culture, information and communication, and food ​and non-alcoholic beverages. Prices for clothing and footwear dipped ‌slightly, ⁠while education and transport showed the lowest increases.
Latin America's fourth-largest economy is facing deteriorating fiscal accounts due to declining revenues and rising ​spending. The ​government of ⁠right-wing President Abelardo De La Espriella, who took office last month, ​is seeking to build a governing ​coalition ⁠from a fragmented right-wing in order to secure a majority in Congress, where the leftist Historic ⁠Pact ​bloc has the largest ​number of seats.
